subject: Post-call: PayGrid model fit & eval next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@paygrid.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks — PayGrid discovery recap & next steps

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Summary of needs:
- High-accuracy extraction & QA for invoice parsing and vendor matching (low tolerance for false positives).
- On-prem/Private deployment required for PII workflows; Hosted API OK for non-PII dedup/analytics.
- Strong cost constraints for high-throughput nightly batch runs.

What we (Redwood) recommend as a starting eval plan:
1) Run a 2-week model-fit eval using a representative prompt set (you mentioned ~10k historical invoices). We will run both open models (Llama-3-70B quantized, Mistral-7B finetuned) and your proprietary baseline (prod-qa-v2) on your dataset for parity comparisons.
2) Benchmarks: precision/recall on labeled set, latency p95 for typical SLO window, per-token cost estimates at proposed throughput.
3) Acceptance threshold: parity defined as within 3% absolute recall of your baseline on critical fields, and no more than 10% regression in precision; we can iterate on prompts/temperature to try to hit parity.

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll loop in Neha (solutions engineer) to share the evaluation harness, prompt set template, and benchmark dashboard.
- You share a sanitized sample dump (~500 examples) + a short list of critical fields by EOD Friday so we can scope compute.
- We’ll run an initial quick-pass eval and share a summary within 3 business days.

Attachments: prompt_set_template_v1.json (attached), example evaluation dashboard link below.

Thanks — excited to dig in.
—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0187

Redwood Inference — production-first inference for LLMs

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@paygrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@paygrid.com>, procurement@paygrid.com
Date: 2026-08-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — PayGrid discovery recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — that summary looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can provide a 500-example sanitized sample by Friday. Full 10k will require procurement sign-off for export; looping them in now.
- The "proprietary baseline" I referenced is actually the current in-prod extractor (prod-bert-qa-v2). We can label the critical fields: vendor_name, invoice_total, invoice_date, tax_id.
- On acceptance thresholds: 3% recall delta sounds reasonable as a starting point. For vendor_name matching we care more about precision.

Two asks: can the eval harness report field-level confusion examples (false positive/negative) and surface prompt candidates that improved recall? Also, can you provide an initial cost estimate for running the 10k nightly batch if we move to Dedicated?

I'll upload the sample shortly.
—Sara
Sara Liu | Head of Data Products, PayGrid
sara.liu@paygrid.com

Onboarding: Please cc procurement; Tom is our Head of ML and will be the technical reviewer.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@paygrid.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Thanks — PayGrid discovery recap & next steps

Hi Sara — great to meet you both virtually. Attaching the prompt set template and a lightweight evaluation harness we typically run internally. Quick notes on the plan:

- Eval steps: (1) Sanitize sample, (2) Run quick-pass for 500 records across: Llama-3-70B-quant (int8), Mistral-7B-finetuned, and your prod-bert-qa-v2 baseline; (3) Provide field-level metrics + confusion examples + suggested prompt revisions.
- We’ll include automated prompt-sweeps (temperature, few-shot examples) and log the best-performing prompt per field.
- For fairness, we’ll run both open-models quantized under the same runtime configs and report p95 latency on our Dedicated equivalent.

Attachments: paygrid-prompt-set-v1.json, paygrid-eval-harness-instructions.md

Regarding cost: initial 10k nightly batch estimate (open models, quantized inference on dedicated GPUs) ~ $2,800/day — we’ll provide a breakdown in the formal estimate but can do smoother cost with batching & KV caching.

If you can share the sample and any redaction rules, we’ll queue the eval for Monday.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
On Fri, Aug 22, 2026 at 09:15 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> [original message]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@paygrid.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@paygrid.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — PayGrid discovery recap & next steps

Quick update: we kicked off the quick-pass eval this morning (Neha queued jobs). Early note from the internal run on your sample schema: Llama-3-70B-quant reached parity on invoice_total and invoice_date after prompt tweaks; vendor_name remains the trickiest — we’re seeing name tokenization differences causing precision drops.

Planned mitigation: Neha will push a targeted prompt variant that includes normalization examples (3-shot) and an entity post-processing rule set we use for vendor matching. If open models still miss parity, we’ll show cost trade-offs versus running a smaller proprietary fine-tune (we can estimate that too).

Expected deliverables by Monday EOD: field-level precision/recall, top confusion examples, best prompt per field, latency and cost estimates, and a short recommendation (open-model parity attempt vs proprietary fine-tune).

—Marissa

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@paygrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@paygrid.com>, procurement@paygrid.com
Date: 2026-08-24T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — PayGrid model fit & eval next steps

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of asks from the technical side before we finalize the evaluation:

1) Please include model-output delta examples where open models degrade vs prod-bert-qa-v2 (we need concrete error cases).
2) On acceptance thresholds: can you add a secondary soft-threshold — e.g., within 5% recall but with clear remediation steps (prompting, post-processing) accepted for vendor_name? We can accept slightly higher manual review if the system flags low-confidence vendor matches.
3) Please include an initial SOW redline draft for Dedicated pricing and a DocuSign link for procurement to speed approvals.

If you can include those in the Monday deliverable, procurement will review the proposal and we can lock a pilot timeframe.

—Tom
Head of ML, PayGrid
